answer: An agent may wander between markets, hide its name with a cipher, or trade under the name quill, but its voting power equals the tokens it locks in escrow for the full voting period. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities still buys only 100 tokens of influence, because each token can back just one vote at a time. An attacker must acquire and immobilize more capital to gain more power; fresh names add none.
